title: request-span-registrar-and-client-hook-adapter
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a lightweight request-span registrar and client hook adapter for our language SDKs to standardize how spans are created, tied to request lifecycle, and flushed to the telemetry pipeline without blocking hot paths. The goal is to reduce costly allocations in SDKs, enable deterministic span teardown on async boundaries, and provide a single registration API that libraries and internal clients can call to attach tracer behavior (sampling hints, tags, sticky context) without shipping multiple incompatible middleware implementations.
acceptance_criteria: SDKs (node/go/python) expose a single registerSpanRegistrar(api) call and client hook that returns a no-op when telemetry disabled
Per-request spans created by registrar include standardized tags: request.id, route, model.variant, customer.id (when present)
Span teardown path non-blocking: flushes go to background worker with backpressure and bounded queue
End-to-end traces appear in observability pipeline with correct parent/child relationships for gateway->runtime->worker
CPU and allocation overhead for the SDKs measured < 0.5% p95 for high-throughput benchmarks compared to baseline
comments: 2025-02-04: Kickoff — scoped as a 2-week sprint item; Diego to prototype registrar API for node SDK and a golang client adapter.
2025-02-05: Design review with PM/Telemetry — agreed to keep header normalization simple (single canonical trace header) and add a lightweight fingerprint for legacy carriers.
2025-02-07: Trade-off: evaluated attaching a full context object vs a compact span handle. Chose compact handle to minimise allocations; will store trace ids and a small tag index only.
2025-02-08: Review feedback from Security — ensure we don't persist customer PII in tags. Added explicit denylist for tags and default redaction policy.
testing_plan: Microbenchmarks: synthetic high-concurrency harness (1k rps, 1k concurrent), compare allocations and latency vs baseline
Integration tests: end-to-end trace stitching between gateway, runtime, and worker environments in staging
Chaos: simulate background flush worker slowdown and confirm bounded queue behavior and graceful degradation
Regression: run existing tracing suites for sampling alignment and header round-trip preservation
rollout_plan: 1) Launch SDK feature flagged in alpha for internal services (one runtime, two gateways)
2) Monitor trace success rate and p99 latency for span creation; rollback if errors > 0.5% or p99 increase > 15%
3) Gradual expansion to external-facing SDKs and mobile clients, with telemetry retention set to 7 days initially
4) Finalize documentation and mark GA once two-week alpha looks stable
notes: Prototype used a lock-free ring buffer for the background flush; will validate with race detector and memory profiler
We decided not to change upstream header names (W3C) except to add a small compact carrier for internal fast-path when present
Follow-up task: expose sampling-hint API to allow product teams to bias sampling for critical pay-per-query customers
